summary: For 2001-2025, the satellite record over the Douala box shows no statistically significant trend. The estimated change is 14.4 mm per year (95% CI -4.1 to 37.9).
what_it_means: The Mann-Kendall test was used on 25 annual totals. The estimated change is 3.9% per decade relative to the mean annual total of 3724 mm.
what_it_does_not_mean: This result says nothing about why rainfall behaves this way. It says nothing about future years. A result that is not significant is not evidence that rainfall stayed the same. The value is an average over an area, not a reading at one point.
limitations: The satellite constellation changed in 2014 (TRMM to GPM), which can create artifacts that look like a trend.
IMERG has lower skill near the coast, and Douala sits on the Wouri estuary.
With 25 annual values the test has low statistical power.
The numbers are a satellite estimate averaged over a box of about 33 km, not a local reading.
